input.quote: 21.1 Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the Fees paid or payable by Customer under the first Order Form during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim. The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims.
input.rationale: §21 is otherwise at the preferred position: the cap is expressly mutual, §21.2 mutually excludes indirect and consequential damages, §21.3 makes confidentiality, data-protection and security breaches, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and infringement of the other Party's IP uncapped Excluded Claims, and Customer's payment obligation is expressly not damages. The single material failure is the cap measure: "Fees" is defined (§1.5–1.6) as the one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee stated in the first Order Form, and §21.1 further confines recovery to that first Order Form, so the cap is illusory and far below six months' fees — walk-away territory. Our single edit resets the basis to the greater of the fees (including subscription fees) paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement and all Order Forms in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000, using the preferred claim-based lookback anchor and lowercase "fees" so the narrow definition is not re-imported. §§21.2–21.3 are untouched.

proposal.summary: §21.1 cap: greater of fees paid or payable in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] The cap is illusory because "Fees" is the one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee under the first Order Form only, so we reset the mutual cap to the greater of the fees (including subscription fees) paid or payable in the twelve months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000. Mutuality, the indirect-damages exclusion and the uncapped Excluded Claims in §21 are unchanged.
